value.first: Week 1: don't fight the pasta and crackers, just widen around them. At each meal put her safe food on the plate plus one small new thing next to it - a few peas, a strip of chicken, a slice of cucumber. No pressure to eat it, no bites required. At 4 she's allowed to just look at it and touch it. Expect her to ignore the new food most days. That's normal and it's still working.
value.second: Weeks 2-3: give her a job. Let her pour her own crackers, scoop pasta onto her plate, help stir something at the counter. Kids this age eat more of what they helped make. Keep serving that one new food alongside - it can take 10 or 15 exposures before a preschooler tries a bite, so keep it coming without comment. Eat it yourself in front of her; she copies more than she admits.
value.third: By week 4 you're looking for her to touch, lick, or nibble new things - not clean her plate. Trust her appetite: your job is what and when, hers is whether and how much. Some days she'll eat almost nothing but pasta and that's a normal preschool week. If she's dropping weight, gagging or choking on textures, or the list of foods keeps shrinking rather than slowly growing, that's worth raising with your doctor.
